outcomes.blurb: The editor plan, with Grok Bot and cloud agents.
outcomes.routing: Use Grok 4.7 at standard speed for bulk edits (fast mode is the default and costs 2x). Switch to Sonnet 5.5 or Opus 5.5 from the Other Models pool for hard infra, at API prices. Let Grok Bot run routines and launch cloud agents.

outcomes.blurb: More Cursor and Grok Bot usage in one bill.
outcomes.routing: Same as Cursor Pro, with a bigger pool: Grok 4.7 at standard speed for bulk work, Claude models for hard infra, Grok Bot as the hub.

outcomes.blurb: One bill, the highest Grok Bot allowance and $400 of third-party models.
outcomes.routing: Lean on Cursor's own models (Composer 2.5, Grok 4.7) for routine work so the $400 third-party pool lasts; spend it on Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 for hard work. No Claude Code or Codex plan is included.

outcomes.blurb: Claude Code with the strongest coding scores, at the entry price.
outcomes.routing: Run Sonnet 5.5 at high or max effort by default (index 68.4 at max vs 45.9 at medium). Use Opus 5.5 when stuck; it drains quota fastest. Use /clear between tasks.

outcomes.blurb: Our report's pick if you can pay for only one agent plan.
outcomes.routing: Sonnet 5.5 by default, Opus 5.5 for multi-day work, long refactors and client writing. Keep bot-driven runs on an API key.

outcomes.blurb: The safer Claude tier if your use stays heavy.
outcomes.routing: Sonnet 5.5 by default, Opus 5.5 orchestrating long work. Keep bot-driven runs on an API key with a budget.

outcomes.blurb: Codex at the entry price, the most usage per dollar.
outcomes.routing: GPT-6.1 Sol by default ($2 / $10, index about 63). GPT-6 Luna for cheap checkable chores ($0.10 / $0.50). Skip GPT-5.6 Terra for new work; there is no GPT-6.1 Terra.

outcomes.blurb: Codex without a five-hour cap, plus your first dot.
outcomes.routing: GPT-6.1 Sol by default, Luna for chores, Astra ($10 / $50) only when you need its long context or computer use; it costs 5x Sol for about the same coding score.

outcomes.blurb: No plan: pay per token on Anthropic and OpenAI keys.
outcomes.routing: Luna for bulk and bot jobs, Sonnet 5.5 for hard turns, Opus 5.5 sparingly. Put a hard monthly cap on each key.

outcomes.blurb: Grok Bot and the editor, plus Claude Code for hard work.
outcomes.routing: Grok 4.7 at standard speed in Cursor for bulk edits, Claude Code with Sonnet 5.5 (Opus 5.5 when stuck) for hard infra. Grok Bot is the hub.

outcomes.blurb: Grok Bot and the editor, plus Codex volume.
outcomes.routing: Codex on GPT-6.1 Sol by default, Luna for chores, Grok 4.7 in Cursor for bulk edits. Borrow Claude models from the Cursor pool for hard infra.

outcomes.blurb: A three-plan stack: Grok Bot hub, Codex workhorse, Claude specialist.
outcomes.routing: Codex on GPT-6.1 Sol by default, GPT-6 Luna for chores, Claude Code by hand (Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 when stuck) for hard infra, Grok 4.7 at standard speed in Cursor for bulk edits. Grok Bot is the hub.

outcomes.blurb: Our report's main pick: Claude Max 5x, and keep Cursor Pro for Grok Bot.
outcomes.routing: Sonnet 5.5 by default in Claude Code, Opus 5.5 for long and open-ended work, Grok 4.7 at standard speed in Cursor for bulk. Point bot jobs at a capped Luna API key.

outcomes.blurb: Codex at Pro limits and dots, plus Grok Bot.
outcomes.routing: Codex on GPT-6.1 Sol by default, Luna for chores, Grok Bot as the team hub and a dot as a phone front door. Claude models from the Cursor pool for hard infra.

outcomes.blurb: The volume-first stack from our report: Codex at Pro limits, Cursor hub, Claude specialist.
outcomes.routing: Codex on Sol as the default runner with automatic PR review, Luna for routine edits, Claude Code by hand for hard problems, Grok Bot for routines and cloud agents.

unverified_general: Cursor's Cursor Models pool size and Grok Bot weekly usage per tier are not published.
Codex Pro weekly limits and the differences between the $100, $200 and $500 tiers are not published.
Whether Claude Max 5x or 20x holds a heavy pace is not confirmed; Anthropic publishes multipliers, not dollar allowances.
AA Coding Agent Index values were read from the BenchLM mirror, not AA's own page.
GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra Terminal-Bench 4.0 scores came from a search snippet and a third-party summary.
Dots limits after the first month are not published.
Fit values (0 to 1) are our editorial judgments, each tied to the fact shown next to it.
